title: Which cubes fit the box without gaps?
description: A box is twelve, eighteen and thirty six centimetres long, wide and high, and cubes must pack it without gaps. The highest common factor of the three measures gives the sides that fit, and the choices are checked one by one.
teaching_notes: One idea: a cube packs a box without gaps only when its side divides the length, the width and the height, so the side is a common factor of all three. Ask the class to try one cube side on all three edges before the working is shown. Watch for students who test a side on the length only.

source: End of chapter Figure it Out, Q6
video_script.why: The child has used the highest common factor to cut lengths into equal pieces and now uses it for the sides of cubes that pack a box.
video_script.substitution: Find the highest common factor of the three measures of the box, list its factors, and test each cube side from the choices.
video_script.anchor: A box drawn with length 12 cm, width 18 cm and height 36 cm, with small cubes of different sides beside it.
video_script.payoff_line: The cubes of six, three and two centimetres fit

final_answer.spoken: the cubes of six, three and two centimetres

never_show: 9 cm or 4 cm as a cube that fits
maths_rules: a cube packs an edge without gaps only if its side divides that edge
side must divide 12, 18 and 36, so it is a common factor of all three
9 does not divide 12 and 4 does not divide 18; 6, 3, 2 divide 12, 18 and 36
video_script.design: One idea: the cube side is a common factor of the three measures. The box stays on the board and the highest common factor is built from the prime counts.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>A box has length twelve centimetres, width eighteen centimetres and height thirty six centimetres.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>We want to pack it with cubes, without leaving gaps.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>The cubes have sides of nine, six, four, three or two centimetres.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>Which of these cubes fit?

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Cubes fill a line without a gap when the side goes into the line exactly.

<bookmark mark='m3'/>The largest number that divides all of them is called their highest common factor.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, the side of the cube must divide twelve, eighteen and thirty six.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: 12 = 2 × 2 × 3, 18 = 2 × 3 × 3, 36 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3; smaller counts give 2 × 3, so HCF = 6

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, twelve is two times two times three. Eighteen is two times three times three.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Thirty six is two times two times three times three.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The smaller counts give two times three. The highest common factor is six.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, the common factors are the factors of six. They are one, two, three and six.
